chapters.intro: Your people have crossed the mountains with little more than seed grain and bronze sickles. The valley is green, the neighbour quiet, and the first winter is coming. See that there is bread.
chapters.outro: The granaries are full. Word of a valley that feeds its people spreads over the passes, and more settlers come.

mission.name: Chapter 1: The First Winter
mission.story: A green valley, a quiet neighbour, and hungry settlers. Grow wheat, grind it and bake bread before the first winter's end.

do.text: Your people have stopped at last. {1}, lord of the next valley, sends word that he wants no quarrel with you. Sow the fields before the frost comes.
do.title: The valley

do.text: The millstones turn. Flour means bread, and bread means nobody starves this winter.
The first frost whitens the fields. {1} sends a cart of grain as a sign of friendship.
do.title: First frost

chapters.new: Copper, tin and bronze; tools and arms by metal
chapters.intro: The eastern hills hold copper, and tin lies further off. Melt them together and you have bronze: better tools and sharper blades. Two neighbours have the same idea.
chapters.outro: Bronze rings from your forges, and your warriors carry its blades. The veterans of the hill war follow you.

mission.name: Chapter 2: Bronze and Tin
mission.story: Mine copper and tin, melt bronze and arm your warriors with it before a jealous neighbour comes for the hills.

do.text: Copper in the eastern hills, tin further off. A geologist finds where the ore lies; a bronze foundry melts the two together over charcoal.
do.title: Bronze and Tin

do.text: {2} has heard of your foundry. His envoys came to trade and stayed to count your warriors.
{2} wants your bronze and has come to take it. Arm your warriors!
do.title: War in the hills

do.text: Kinsmen from over the mountains have heard of the war. Four warriors come to stand with you.

chapters.new: Iron working and the Roman age
chapters.intro: Your smiths have heard of a black metal harder than bronze. Whoever learns to work it first will rule these hills, and the realm that learns it second will not forgive the first.
chapters.outro: Iron rings from your forges and a new age has begun. Your best soldiers march with you into the next chapter.

mission.name: Chapter 3: The Iron Age
mission.story: Study iron working and reach the Roman age, then dig iron and coal and forge iron weapons. Reaching the new age first will not go unanswered.

do.text: Research gathers in your scriptorium. The study of Iron working opens the Roman age: iron mines, smelters, and weaponsmiths whose blades break bronze.
do.title: The black metal

do.text: A rival realm has learned to work iron. Hurry, or its legions will be first in the hills.
Iron in your hands frightens {1}. His warriors are on the march before your first iron blade is cold.
do.title: The Iron Age

do.text: {2} has no love for {1}, and offers you an alliance against him. You accept.
do.title: An ally

chapters.intro: A broad river splits the land, and the realm across it is at peace with you. Build a market, trade what you have plenty of for what you lack, and bridge the river.
chapters.outro: Carts roll both ways over your bridges. Trade has made friends of strangers, and some of them follow you.

mission.name: Chapter 4: Markets and Bridges
mission.story: Trade with a peaceful neighbour across the river, while a second neighbour watches the carts go by.

do.text: {1}, across the river, has made peace with you and has goods to spare. Build a market, then offer a trade in Diplomacy.
do.title: The river

do.text: {1}'s merchants are pleased with the trade and leave a purse of gold at your market.
{2} envies the trade on your river. His warriors gather at your border.
do.title: Envy

chapters.intro: A hand-made coast: your village in the south, a rich iron ridge in the middle, and to the north a rival with ships. The sea is a road for both of you.
chapters.outro: The coast is yours. Ships carry your banner along every shore.

mission.name: Chapter 5: The Iron Coast
mission.story: Hold the iron ridge, open a harbour, and take one rival realm, while fleets from the north land on your shore.

do.text: The iron ridge lies between you and {1}. Whoever holds it has iron for a generation. Keep soldiers near the beaches: {1} has ships.
do.title: The Iron Coast

do.text: Your harbour is open. A shipyard builds ships, and ships carry soldiers waiting at your headquarters to a rival's shore: attack a building near the coast.
Sails on the horizon! {1} comes by sea.
do.title: Sails

chapters.new: Taverns, chapels and a wonder: the great hall
chapters.intro: A long war leaves people weary. Give them taverns and a chapel, and raise a great hall where the whole realm can feast, and see the town work with a will again.
chapters.outro: Music from the great hall carries over the rooftops. Content people work harder, and your realm has never been richer.

mission.name: Chapter 6: The Great Hall
mission.story: Make your people content, and build the realm's first wonder: a great hall.

goals.text: Build a wonder: the great hall

do.text: The new kingdoms have come. Your people want beer and bread in the taverns, candles in the chapel, and a hall worthy of the realm. A wonder is built once, and helps for good.
do.title: Feast days

do.text: Songs from the taverns. People come from far off to see the feast days, and some of them stay.
{2} sends raiders to spoil the feast.
do.title: Raiders

do.text: The great hall stands! Lords and craftsmen from far away bring gifts.
do.title: The great hall

chapters.intro: The towns are growing rich, and their craftsmen have learned that a trade worked side by side works faster. The old lords do not like the free towns at all.
chapters.outro: The guild towns stand, and the cathedral's bells ring over them. The old lords have learned to leave the towns alone.

mission.name: Chapter 7: The Guild Towns
mission.story: Study Guilds and build workshops of one trade close together, so they form a guild. Raise a cathedral, and keep the lords from the towns.

do.text: High walls and busy streets. Workshops of the same trade near each other form a guild once you know Guilds, and each works faster for it: the more, the faster.
do.title: The guild towns

do.text: The guilds are founded. Build three carpenters close together: they need only planks, and make furniture the nobles want.
{1}'s lords fear the free towns and march to put them in their place.
do.title: The lords

do.text: The cathedral's bells ring out. Pilgrims come, and stay.

chapters.intro: A rival has walled himself in behind towers and castles. Bows and catapults will not break those walls: gunpowder will.
chapters.outro: The walls are down. Only the sea and one last war stand between you and the crown.

mission.name: Chapter 8: Powder and Shot
mission.story: Make gunpowder from sulfur, saltpeter and charcoal, arm musketeers, and break a rival who is already at war with you.

do.text: {1} has declared war, and sits behind his walls. Sulfur and lead mines, a saltpeter works and a powder mill give you gunpowder; a gunsmith makes muskets of it.
do.title: The siege

do.text: {1}'s soldiers come out from behind the walls!
Muskets! Now break {1}'s realm.
do.title: Powder and shot

chapters.new: Warships, naval yards and coastal forts
chapters.intro: You land on a coast of islands, with one ship and a harbour for a headquarters. The two realms here rule the sea, and they will not share it.
chapters.outro: Your warships rule the sea between the islands. The last war is coming, and it will come by land.

mission.name: Chapter 9: Lords of the Sea
mission.story: Build a naval yard and a fleet, guard your coast with forts, and take one realm across the water.

do.text: Your harbour is your headquarters. A naval yard builds warships that sink fleets at sea and guard your landings; a coastal fort fires on ships that come near.
do.title: The islands

do.text: The first warship slides into the water. Keep your fleet escorting your landings.
{1}'s fleet is at sea, and it is coming for you!
do.title: A fleet

chapters.intro: Machines are coming: steam engines that pump mines dry, mills that make steel, and iron roads that carry a train of goods faster than any cart. The realm that builds them first will be the master of the age.
chapters.outro: Trains run on your railways, and the halls of your exhibition palace are full of wonders. One crown remains.

mission.name: Chapter 10: Steam and Rails
mission.story: Reach the Industrial age, make steel and join your towns by rail, before a rival does.

goals.text: Build a wonder: the exhibition palace

do.text: The Age of Reason is here. Your scholars point the way: the Dawn of industry, then the steam engine, then railways. Steel mills need iron and coal; stations join your towns by rail.
do.title: The age of machines

do.text: The Industrial age! Show the world what your realm can make: build an exhibition palace.
do.title: Industry

do.text: A rival realm has reached the Industrial age. Its factories smoke day and night.
{1} wants your coal and iron.
do.title: War

do.text: Railways! A steel mill's steel and a rolling mill's rails make the iron road. Merchants send steel to help you start.

chapters.intro: Three realms remain, and only one crown. The lords have sworn to stop you together. Hold the Hearthlands.
chapters.outro: The Hearthlands are one realm under your banner. The chronicle ends here, but the land will remember.

mission.name: Chapter 11: The Crown of the Hearthlands
mission.story: Three strong rivals, sworn to stop you. Defeat them all.

do.text: {1}, {2} and {3} have sworn to stop you. They will not wait long.
do.title: The crown

do.text: The three lords keep their oath: all three are at war with you.
do.title: The oath

do.text: One banner is down! Soldiers who served the fallen lord come over to you.
Only one lord still stands against you. Finish it.
do.title: The last lord
